# Overview

The Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) profiled the
proteomes of several hundred TCGA tumors. `CPTACdata` downloads those data
from the Proteomic Data Commons (PDC) and appends them to a
`MultiAssayExperiment` from `curatedTCGAData`.

```{r load-packages, message = FALSE}
library(CPTACdata)
library(curatedTCGAData)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
```

# Which TCGA projects have CPTAC data?

```{r list-cptac-projects}
cptacProjects
```

# Appending to a MultiAssayExperiment

Start with any `curatedTCGAData` object for one TCGA project. Only patients
in its `colData` can be matched, so include enough assays to cover the
patients of interest.

```{r fetch-tcga-mae, message = FALSE}
mae <- curatedTCGAData("OV", "RPPAArray", version = "2.1.1", dry.run = FALSE)
```

A dry run reports how many patients each PDC study shares with the object,
downloading only sample metadata:

```{r dry-run}
appendCPTAC(mae, dry_run = TRUE)
```

Then add the data. The project is detected from `colData`, and the
**proteome is added by default**. Call `appendCPTAC()` again for other assay
types:

```{r append-experiments}
mae <- appendCPTAC(mae)
mae <- appendCPTAC(mae, fraction = "Phosphoproteome")
mae
```

The new experiments have one column per TCGA sample, and the `sampleMap`
links them to patients:

```{r sample-map}
tail(sampleMap(mae))
mae[["CPTAC_PNNL_Proteome"]]
```

The JHU and PNNL ovarian proteomes are separate experiments that share some
patients:

```{r upset-samples, eval = FALSE}
upsetSamples(mae)
```

```{r upset-samples-figure, echo = FALSE}
img_path <-
    if (knitr::opts_knit$get("child")) "man/figures/" else "../man/figures/"
knitr::include_graphics(paste0(img_path, "CPTACdata_upset.png"))
```
